deck: Week 3: Arfan goes 3-0 with Brock Bowers on his bench, Haroon cashes the weekly high for the second straight week, Bilal's Gibbs scores 37.9 and the chat decides he's inherited Asim's powers, Achane's season ends in the first quarter, and the commissioner, alone at 0-3, trades for Jonathan Taylor under a veto rule he declined to change. It's also the week the board changed: from here on, about 70 percent of every ranking is what actually happened.

teams.biggestDevelopment: 3-0 with Bowers' 22.6 and Wilson's 20.4 on the bench.

movementReasons.reason: 3-0 and 27-6 all-play, best in the league

teams.headline: UNDEFEATED, UNSUPERVISED
teams.verdict: 3-0 with 56.5 points on the bench, including a tight end he didn't know was playing.
teams.analysis:
Arfan beat the commissioner 109.14 to 94.68 and made it look optional. Joe Burrow threw three touchdowns for 22.58, Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10 balls for 30.36, and Derrick Henry scored twice for 21.4. Meanwhile Brock Bowers, back from injury, scored 22.6 on the bench while Dalton Kincaid started and scored 2.8. Arfan's explanation, filed Sunday afternoon: "Bro i Benched him. Didn't know until after 12pm games." Michael Wilson added 20.4 on the same bench, and the Eagles defense finished at −1.0.

None of it mattered, which is the scariest thing about this team. HNFNR is 27-6 against the field through three weeks, the best mark in the league, and leads all 12 teams in wins. On Friday the commissioner wished aloud that Arfan would score 150 and he'd score 155, then revised it to 154. Arfan replied, "I already know this thread going in the next AI drop." It is in the drop, next to the final score.

Under the new rules, waiver hits and player performance count toward the ceiling, and this roster earns the jump from 10th to 2nd: Bowers is healthy, Denzel Boston and Dalton Schultz both came off waivers as usable starters, and Smith-Njigba is playing like a first-rounder. Next is Kashir, without Justin Jefferson.

teams.biggestDevelopment: The weekly high again — $200 cashed, still $167 down on the buy-in.
teams.headline: THE HUNDO, AGAIN
teams.verdict: 138.48 and the week high for the second straight Sunday. The champ is $200 into a $367 hole.
teams.analysis:
Brock Purdy threw four touchdowns for 31.28, George Kittle, promoted from the bench to starting tight end, scored 23.2, and Ja'Marr Chase and Christian Watson added 20.3 and 19.1. Team Noor put 138.48 on Ivan, won by 42.26, and took the weekly $100 for the second week in a row. Haroon has now collected $200 against a $367 buy-in. He's still down $167, and he and Arfan are the only managers who have cashed anything.

It was close. Haroon, Sunday night: "Damn. Almost had highest points total. Oh I still have a chance if it goes to OT." He finished 2.14 ahead of Bilal. Monday morning Bilal arrived with the evil eye: "Dangggg back to back Haroon I see you! Your team looks so so amazing." Haroon's reply is the most confident sentence of the week: "I survived Asim last year."

The waiver move of the week belongs here too. Haroon added Jared Goff, who scored 19.36 on the bench. That's the same Goff whose Christmas-week collapse handed Haroon the 2025 title, and the same Goff Asim dropped in Week 1. The only worry is Breece Hall, who is week-to-week with a quad injury. The roster behind him is the reason Noor now holds the No. 1 ceiling.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Gibbs scored three TDs; MBK missed the hundo by 2.14.

movementReasons.reason: Results now weigh 70% of the board
Stafford benched again; Jacobs still no timeline

teams.headline: THE POWERS HAVE TRANSFERRED
teams.verdict: Gibbs scored 37.9, the chat blamed Bilal for every injury, and MBK missed the hundo by 2.14.
teams.analysis:
Jahmyr Gibbs scored three touchdowns and 37.9 points, the best individual game of the week, and Team MBK beat Kashir 136.34 to 106.68. Drake London added 23.9, Dak Prescott 18.94, and Tee Higgins 18.0. That was 10-1 against the field. It's MBK's best week of the season, and it still finished 2.14 short of Haroon for the $100.

The bigger story is supernatural. Mid-game, Bilal told Kashir, "Bro Kashi just go down damn it!!!" Justin Jefferson then left with an ankle injury, and Kashir filed the complaint: "Bro now he got me JJ out for the game wtf. Bilal bro stop." Kashir's ruling: "Bilal might be the new Asim." Asim conceded the title on the spot: "I'll see yall next season boys. Bilal got me this year." Arfan named the league: "Kala jadu league."

Two housekeeping notes. Matthew Stafford scored 20.9 on the bench, one week after scoring 26.98 there, and Bilal is still selling him to Naafay, who he plays next. And on Tuesday morning Bilal dropped Chris Brooks, the Green Bay handcuff this desk praised in Week 2 as "the contingency's contingency." The desk withdraws the compliment. Jacobs still has no timeline, and MBK's ceiling rises to 3rd on what Gibbs, London and Higgins are doing without him.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Jefferson's ankle injury projects to a Week 8 return.

movementReasons.reason: Jefferson's ankle — out until about Week 8

teams.headline: THE DARNOLD SUNDAY
teams.verdict: Added Sam Darnold at 10:48 Sunday morning, benched him, and watched him score 27.66.
teams.analysis:
At 10:48 AM Sunday, Kashir picked up Sam Darnold. At noon, he started Jordan Love. Love scored 18.48; Darnold scored 27.66 on the bench. It didn't decide the game, since Team MBK won by 29.66, but after two straight weeks of correct quarterback calls, this one went the other way. Love's 18.48 also came in a 35-14 loss to Drake London's Falcons. On Friday, Kashir had filed his only prediction of the week: "I'm glad Drake London decided to Show up the week I played you." London scored 23.9.

The real damage is Justin Jefferson's ankle. He left after two catches, and the projection is a return around Week 8. With Amon-Ra St. Brown held to 9.9, this receiver-built team is suddenly one receiver short for a month. The all-play record still says contender: 25-8, second-best in the league. He lost this week at 7-4, which is bad luck, not a bad team.

Kashir also spent the week as the league's reform caucus: cut bench spots from seven to five, switch waivers to a FAB bidding system, and "High key we need to reduce the bench spots." He even diagnosed Bazaan's roster through it: "FAB would gave u a chance." The commissioner's response, Tuesday morning: "I aint changing no rules." Next is HNFNR, the only undefeated team, without Jefferson.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Traded Bryce Young for Adonai Mitchell, who was ruled out right away.
teams.headline: LAMAR, OFF THE BLOCK
teams.verdict: Put him up for trade last Sunday, got 20.44 this Sunday, and started the right defense this time.
teams.analysis:
One week after "He sucks. Lamar up for trade," Lamar Jackson threw two touchdowns for 20.44 and Bazan beat Bizzy 100.94 to 84.70. James Cook added 19.4, Juwan Johnson 19.3, and Chase McLaughlin 12.0. Last week's post-mortem ("if only I started panthers d") was acted on: the Panthers defense started and scored 6.0, and the Cardinals defense scored −4.0 on the bench.

The quarterback room remains a curiosity. Bo Nix scored 24.14 on the bench, and Kashir asked the obvious question: "Brother why do you have 3 qbs." Bazaan answered with "🤫" and then "Just trust the process." The process involved trading Bryce Young to Yaseen for Adonai Mitchell, who was ruled out almost immediately: "Course Adonai is hurt when I trade for him." Then Jalen Coker went down with a quad injury: "N now Coker 😭 all my WRs getting hurt."

That receiver attrition is why the ceiling slides from 4th to 7th, even as the board moves Bazan up to 5th. A.J. Brown is still on IR until around Week 6, Nabers managed 5.1, and the receiver corps is currently Sutton plus whoever is healthy. Next is Gang Green, the trade partner, one week after the deal.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Achane tore his ACL in the first quarter; dropped Tuesday.
teams.headline: 2-1 AND COPING
teams.verdict: Won at 2-9 against the field, lost Achane for the season, and the man who drafted him called it an upgrade.
teams.analysis:
Gang Green beat Asim 88.54 to 84.46 with the third-lowest score of the week, which is the definition of a lucky win: 2-9 against the field. De'Von Achane scored 1.7, tore his ACL in the first quarter, and was dropped Tuesday morning. On Saturday, the day before, Yaseen had filed this: "Drafting Achane will be my downfall." After the injury, he pivoted: "Honestly might work for the better lol. Won't be forced to start Achane every week." Arfan: "Dang this sounds like coping."

The other storyline is the quarterback trade. Yaseen sent Adonai Mitchell to Bazan for Bryce Young, started Young (13.64), and benched Trevor Lawrence, who scored 19.78. Kashir took Bazan's side of the review: "Yassen how dare you rob my cousin like that. In broad day light." Garrett Wilson (21.7) and waiver-add Kenyon Sadiq (20.0) carried the day, and Harold Fannin Jr. scored 20.6 on the bench because this roster leaves one good game in the shed every week without fail.

The new math is generous to a 2-1 record, so Gang Green holds at 8th. The ceiling isn't: losing Achane drops it from 5th to 10th, and Chuba Hubbard is now the whole backfield plan. Yaseen's own read: "I'll be alright lol." Next is Bazan, the trade partner.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Lost 96.22 to 138.48; Lloyd got four carries.

movementReasons.reason: Results now weigh 70% of the board

teams.headline: WRONG PLACE, WRONG CHAMP
teams.verdict: Lost to the week high by 42.26 and took a 14-19 all-play record into the new math.
teams.analysis:
Ivan scored 96.22, the eighth-best score of the week, and drew the one team that put up 138.48. Christian McCaffrey (19.6), Jeremiyah Love (19.4) and Chris Olave (15.2) played their part. Jalen Hurts managed 12.62 in a 27-7 loss, and with Dallas Goedert ruled out, the replacement tight end, T.J. Hockenson, scored 2.1.

The detail that matters for December is in the backfield. MarShawn Lloyd, whose inherited Green Bay job prompted this desk's formal Week 1 apology, got four carries and scored 2.8 on the bench. The job looks thinner than it did three weeks ago. Ivan also added Carnell Tate off waivers after Bizzy let him go; Tate scored 8.8 on the bench.

The move from 6th to 7th is mostly the method. With results now weighing about 70 percent, a 1-2 record with a 14-19 all-play mark is a 7th-place résumé, and the ceiling slips from 6th to 8th for the same reasons. Ivan, per custom, said nothing in the chat. Next is Bizzy's first game with CeeDee Lamb.

teams.biggestDevelopment: First win behind Bijan's 194 rushing yards.

movementReasons.reason: Penix and Watson cover the QB spot
Caleb out three to four weeks

teams.headline: THE BIJAN BUILD, FINALLY BUILT
teams.verdict: Bijan ran for 194 yards, Penix held the fort, and Naafay got his first win with Watson on the bench.
teams.analysis:
Bijan Robinson ran for 194 yards and two touchdowns, scored 34.3, and IVaafay beat RN 110.24 to 98.74 for its first win of the season: 9-2 against the field, third-best score of the week. Mustafa had announced his rooting interest on Wednesday: "I just want naafay to lose this week." Javonte Williams added 17.3 and Davante Adams 17.2.

The quarterback story is a group project. Naafay missed on both waiver targets ("Wowww I didn't get any of the 2 qbs i wanted from waivers lol. Young or goff"). Yaseen dropped a hint without naming anyone, and Naafay solved it: "Penix? 🤣 … I told yall. I know football lol." Michael Penix Jr. scored 14.04 in the start. Then Naafay also picked up Deshaun Watson ("In Watson I trust"), who scored 20.26 on the bench, more than Penix.

That quarterback carousel is going to run for a while. Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain and is expected to miss three to four weeks, longer than Naafay's hope of "the week after next or maybe even next." IVaafay jumps from 12th to 8th. Next is Team MBK, whose owner has been trying to sell Naafay a quarterback all month and will now try to beat him instead.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Traded Jonathan Taylor to RamBam for CeeDee Lamb and Chase Brown.

movementReasons.reason: Traded Jonathan Taylor to the commissioner

teams.headline: THE JT SALE
teams.verdict: Traded Jonathan Taylor to the commissioner, then learned what 70 percent means.
teams.analysis:
Bizzy lost to Bazan 84.70 to 100.94, going 1-10 against the field. Benching Drake Maye worked: Tyler Shough threw four touchdowns for 23.8 while Maye scored 3.76 on the bench. Almost nothing else did. The 49ers defense, added at 2:13 AM Saturday, scored 0.0. Hunter Henry scored 1.0, TreVeyon Henderson 3.4, and Jonathan Taylor 8.2. At 2:58 PM Sunday Nabil conceded, "My team is shottt," and "Gg @Bazaan."

Then on Monday night came the trade: Taylor, Henderson and Emanuel Wilson to the commissioner for CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown and Emmett Johnson. Nabil: "It was sad letting JT go but had to some cause my team trash. Hopefully helps both of us." Kashir's review: "two first rounders for JT basically, and Nabil got Nico on bench." Bazaan: "Cd n k9 on the same team 🥶." Bilal, for the record: "if Henderson doesn't go off it's a scam."

The drop from 3rd to 9th is steep, and most of it is the method. The preseason cushion is gone, and 11-22 all-play with 288.94 points is ninth-place evidence. The ceiling falls from 2nd to 5th: Lamb, Kenneth Walker, Chase Brown and a returning Nico Collins make a December roster, but the quarterback spot doesn't. One week ago Nabil wrote, "Ayy i am still top 3..commish knows ball." Next is Ivan.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Dropped Coleman, Gadsden and Dell in the same minute Tuesday.
teams.headline: THE IHOP DIVISION
teams.verdict: The Vikings defense scored 19 and it still wasn't enough. The last-place punishment is getting booked early.
teams.analysis:
RN lost to IVaafay 110.24 to 98.74, and the best player on the roster was a defense: the Vikings scored 19.0. Patrick Mahomes managed 15.94, Saquon Barkley 8.5, and Omarion Hampton 5.6. No bench swap covers an 11.5-point margin; Kyler Murray's 10.42 was the best of the reserves. It came against the one opponent Mustafa had publicly hoped would lose.

The transaction log was busier than the scoreboard. Mustafa added Jonah Coleman ("my number 1 waiver wire pick") days before Coleman went on IR, spent the week offering "Orlande Gadsen" to anyone listening, and added Tank Dell. Then at 7:54 AM Tuesday he dropped Coleman, Gadsden and Dell in the same minute. Bilal: "Bro @Mustafa not oronde gadsden!!! Are you crazy?!" Asim's Puka-for-Saquon-and-Smith trade offer was declined: "Plus I only have two RBs why would I trade one of them."

There's a bigger thread running underneath all of it. Mustafa suggested the last-place punishment be "IHOP for 48 hours"; Asim raised it to 72 and reserved a seat: "We chillin at the bottom." Next week is RN vs DEDDYBABA, the IHOP Bowl, and Arfan has already requested the rivalry coverage. RN drops to 10th.

teams.biggestDevelopment: 0-3, then traded for Taylor — the veto rule held.

movementReasons.reason: Taylor and Henderson arrive in the trade

teams.headline: THE COMMISSIONER'S TRADE
teams.verdict: 0-3, a hamstring, a Jonathan Taylor trade, and a veto rule he declined to change.
teams.analysis:
The commissioner lost to Arfan 109.14 to 94.68 and is now 0-3, the league's only winless team. It's also the unluckiest: 10-23 against the field, and nearly a full win below what the scores deserved. C.J. Stroud, picked up to cover for Jayden Daniels, scored 11.68. Bilal had already reviewed the move ("I see you picked up a bum"), and Rameel had answered: "If I'm going down this season, let me atleast go down with my qb." Kalif Raymond scored 18.0 on the bench, but even the best possible lineup came up short. Then Travis Etienne left with a hamstring injury that will cost him Week 4 and more.

Monday night he traded CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown and Emmett Johnson to Nabil for Jonathan Taylor, TreVeyon Henderson and Emanuel Wilson. His only comment: "all im gonna say is that last two years ive done a trade, its worked out for me." Two managers voted to veto, Asim among them. Under the setup Mustafa says he built as an earlier commissioner, a trade stands unless everyone vetoes. The chat asked for majority rule instead (Arfan: "1 vote vs 11 and it still goes through? Should be majority"). The current commissioner ruled Tuesday at 8:32 AM: "I aint changing no rules." The desk notes that the rule and the trade have the same beneficiary.

Bilal asked last week why the commissioner's team is "always a developing story." This week it isn't: it's 0-3. He sits 11th, 0.6 points ahead of Asim on the new math, which the desk ran twice. The ceiling drops from 1st to 4th, because a bell-cow running back is a floor and Lamb was the ceiling. Next is Team Noor, and Daniels probably still isn't back.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Lost by 4.08 with McLaurin's 16.7 on the bench.
teams.headline: THE WINNING POINTS WERE ON THE BENCH
teams.verdict: Terry McLaurin scored 16.7 on the bench. The margin was 4.08.
teams.analysis:
Asim lost to Yaseen 88.54 to 84.46, the lowest score of the week, going 0-11 against the field. Josh Allen was mortal for the first time, scoring 16.96 after taking a shot to the knee (a bruise; he's expected to play). The loss came from the lineup screen. Asim started Rashod Bateman (4.7) over Terry McLaurin, who scored 16.7 on the bench. That swap alone wins the game. His explanation: "wtf zay flowers played today?? I thought he was out I started Bateman 🤣." The Broncos defense added 9.0 on the bench for good measure.

Yaseen twisted the knife in real time: "Harvey about to win it for you tonight." Asim: "Lmaooooo I hate you." Puka Nacua missed another game but should return in Week 4. Asim's trade desk stayed open all week: Allen for Bijan and Jordan Mason, Allen for Gibbs "plus another elite talent," and "who wants some chai and my players." The powers, meanwhile, have left the building. "I'll see yall next season boys. Bilal got me this year."

Then the waiver wire handed him the best claim of the season. Asim holds the No. 1 waiver spot the same week Achane tore his ACL, and he spent two days insisting he didn't want Ollie Gordon II. Kashir: "He gonna pick up ollie Gordon 100%." Asim, Tuesday morning: "The way my record lookin right now I don't have any choice but to take Ollie." Mustafa's summary: "Luckbox." He's 12th at 7-26 all-play. Next is RN in the IHOP Bowl.
